title: "Read" in the cave
hook: alone in the cave, he is seized by the angel Jibril, who says one word: read

segments.voice: Yesterday, the cave of Hira, a tiny room of rock above Mecca. Your line was go up to the quiet. Did you find a pocket of it? Today, what happened in that quiet. Day eighty-six.

A night in Ramadan. He's in the cave, alone, the way he's been so many nights. And then, suddenly, he isn't alone. Someone is there, the angel Jibril, though he doesn't know that yet, and the angel says one word. Iqra. Read. Recite. And he answers, honestly: I am not a reader. He had never learned to read or write. The angel takes hold of him and squeezes him, hard, until he can't bear it, then lets go. Read. I am not a reader. Again, the crushing grip. Read. Again: I am not a reader. A third time. And then the angel speaks the words he is to recite.
screen: `A NIGHT IN RAMADAN.` → `IQRA. READ.` → `I AM NOT A READER.`

segments.voice: These are the first words of the Qur'an to come down, according to most Muslim scholars. They open Surah Al-'Alaq, the ninety-sixth. In Pickthall's translation: “Read: In the name of thy Lord Who createth, Createth man from a clot. Read: And it is thy Lord the Most Bountiful Who teacheth by the pen, Teacheth man that which he knew not.” Look at what's inside that. The first word of revelation is a command to read, given to a man who could not read. Iqra comes from the root q-r-', to read, to recite aloud. And from that same root comes the word Qur'an itself: the recitation, the thing that is read aloud. So the first word already names the whole book. Then, in the name of your Lord. Not read anything, anyhow. Read in the name. That's the bismillah from day one of this path, now as the very first instruction. Then who He is: the one who creates, who made the human being from a clinging clot, from almost nothing. And then, twice, the pen. The one who teaches by the pen, who teaches the human being what he did not know. It's striking. A man who couldn't write is given, as his first revelation, a verse about writing and learning. Muslims have taken that seriously for fourteen centuries: libraries, schools, the careful copying of the Qur'an by hand, the idea that seeking knowledge is part of faith. And they remember the night. The Qur'an says it came down in the month of Ramadan, on a night it calls Laylat al-Qadr, the Night of Power, better than a thousand months.
screen: `THE FIRST WORDS TO COME DOWN.` · `IQRA AND QUR'AN: ONE ROOT.` · `IN THE NAME OF THY LORD.` · `WHO TEACHETH BY THE PEN.` · then, large: `READ, IN THE NAME.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: read one line slowly, twice. Take any line that matters to you. A verse, a poem, a sentence from a letter. Or use today's: read, in the name of thy Lord who createth. Read it once, at normal speed. Then read it again, far slower, one word at a time, letting each word land before the next. Notice what you missed the first time. If you pray, you can begin with bismillah, the way the first revelation did. Then rest in the quiet. The bell holds the time.
Iqra. Read, or recite: the first word of the Qur'an to be revealed, from the same root as the word Qur'an itself.
Your line: read, in the name. Today, before you read something that matters, pause for one breath and read it on purpose. Tomorrow, he runs down the mountain. Day eighty-six.

howItsDone: Muslims remember the first revelation during Ramadan, especially in the last ten nights when many seek Laylat al-Qadr; many children learn Surah Al-'Alaq as one of their first surahs.

fork.setup: alone in the cave at night, he hears a command: read. he has never learned to read. what does he say?
fork.reveal: he says honestly, I am not a reader, three times, before the angel recites the first verses to him (Bukhari).

original.note: Arabic: read, recite; from q-r-', the root of Qur'an.

trapdoor: what you thought: an angel told him to read a book.
what it means: iqra, read or recite, the first word of revelation, spoken to a man who could not read, in the name of the Lord who teaches by the pen.
what a scholar hears: iqra and Qur'an share the root q-r-'; his reply, ma ana bi-qari', means I am not a reader; and 97:1 places the night of the first revelation in Laylat al-Qadr.

sources.quoted: Read: In the name of thy Lord Who createth, Createth man from a clot. Read: And it is thy Lord the Most Bountiful Who teacheth by the pen, Teacheth man that which he knew not.

sources.ref: Sahih al-Bukhari 3 (the angel in the cave: read; I am not a reader; three squeezes)
Qur'an 2:185; 97:1–3 (revealed in Ramadan; the Night of Power, better than a thousand months)

notes: Pickthall 96:1–5 quoted from memory; confirm exact wording, capitalization and line breaks.
'According to most Muslim scholars' the first revelation: the majority view (a minority names the opening of Surah 74 or al-Fatiha). Confirm.
'A night in Ramadan': linking the first revelation to Laylat al-Qadr follows 97:1 and 2:185; the exact night is not fixed. Confirm.
The index word is 'iqra' (without the final hamza); kept.
